body:
Every well-known US growth-momentum system has the same four parts. The first is a **market-regime filter**: buy only in confirmed uptrends. The second is a **leadership universe**: strong earnings and sales growth, top-quintile relative strength, and a Stage 2 uptrend near 52-week highs. The third is a **low-risk entry** from a tight base on rising volume. The fourth is a **hard, small stop**, about 7–8% at most and often 3–5%. The rules below are as the authors describe them. Many details are drawn from the books and were not re-verified against primary editions, and online summaries often misquote thresholds.

| System | Core rules (per author) | Stop / exit |
|---|---|---|
| **CAN SLIM** (O'Neil) | Current quarterly EPS ≥25% YoY; Annual EPS growth ≥25% for 3 years, ROE ≥17%; New product/management/high; Supply–demand (volume); Leader, RS ≥80; Institutional sponsorship rising; Market in confirmed uptrend ([AAII](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/william-oneil-can-slim-approach-to-selecting-growth-stocks)) | Cut every loss at 7–8%, no exceptions ([Liberated Stock Trader](https://www.liberatedstocktrader.com/what-is-canslim/)); take profits at 20–25% (book) |
| **Minervini Trend Template / SEPA / VCP** | Price > 150- and 200-DMA; 150 > 200; 200-DMA rising ≥1 month; 50 > 150 and 200; price > 50-DMA; ≥30% above 52-wk low; within 25% of 52-wk high; RS ≥70 ([Chartmill](https://www.chartmill.com/documentation/trading-and-investing/methodologies/523-SEPA-Explained-Mark-Minervinis-Specific-Entry-Point-Analysis-System)). VCP: 2–6 contractions, each about half the prior, volume drying up, buy the pivot | Max 10% stop, average loss ~5–6%, wins 2–3x losses (book) |
| **Weinstein Stage Analysis** | Weekly chart and 30-week MA. Stage 1 base → **Stage 2 breakout on ~2x volume** → Stage 3 top → Stage 4 decline. Buy only Stage 2; market and sector must also be Stage 2 ([MarketInOut](https://www.marketinout.com/stock-screener/stage-2-uptrend/india)) | Below the base, then trail under the 30-week MA; never hold Stage 4 |
| **Qullamaggie** | Breakouts after big moves and 2-week to 2-month tightening; Episodic Pivots on ~10%+ news gaps with heavy volume ([Tikamalma](https://tikamalma.substack.com/p/qullamaggie-swing-trading-setups)) | Stop at low of day; sell ⅓–½ after 3–5 days; trail with the 10/20-DMA; **risk 0.25–0.5%, win rate ~25–30%** ([CTE](https://completetradersedge.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/CTE-Research-Sheet-Kristjan-Kullamagi-market-wizards-next-generation.pdf)) |
| **Darvas / Livermore** | New highs on unusual volume in growing industries; buy box tops or pivotal points; pyramid only into profit, never average down | Just below the box bottom; exit if the stock "doesn't act right" |
| **Market regime (IBD)** | Follow-through day on day 4+ of a rally attempt; **5–6 distribution days in 25 sessions** = uptrend under pressure ([LuxAlgo](https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/distribution-days/)) | Cut exposure as distribution builds |

body:
An illustrative portfolio structure (a synthesis, not a prescription) puts SPIVA's finding to work. If most active funds trail the index, a self-directed investor should hold a **low-cost index core**, with Indian and US exposure, and run active multibagger bets as a **satellite**. Within the satellite, sensible defaults are as follows. Hold 10–20 names. Start positions at 2–4% of the total portfolio. Raise a position to 6–10% only after the thesis is confirmed by earnings delivery. Cap any single name at about 15–20% at cost. Never use margin or F&O on multibagger theses. Mayer's rule applies to *your* balance sheet as well as the company's: avoid leverage so that drawdowns are not permanent. Indian tax rules reinforce patience. Since July 2024, listed-equity **STCG is 20% and LTCG is 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year** after 12 months' holding ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/finance/personal-finance/budget-2024-all-the-key-changes-to-capital-gains-tax-explained-124072500330_1.html)). Churn is taxed hardest.

body:
IMCL's ~54% ROIC rests on land leased at ₹1/month; the lease expired Jul-2023 and the government counterparty opposes renewal
in the Supreme Court — yet the FY26 annual report never mentions the expiry. **Rule:** for any government-granted input (land,
lease, licence, PPP), record expiry, the obligation given in return and compliance with it, and the counterparty's own filings;
treat the stock as an option on renewal. Add "material external fact absent from the AR" as a disclosure flag. Read vote results
as promoter shares held vs votes polled (a co-promoter abstaining revealed the broken JV). Card v1.3's survival cap cannot see
legal/licence risk → candidate manual trigger. Tail anchoring can *lower* well-documented tails; flag when it does.
Process: sector frames need a full industry map (NSE index lists left 60% of the band unclassified).

- **Nothing in the paper calls.** All calls keep their original probability and date, so the Brier scores test what we actually said.
- **NVIDIA (US-NVDA)**: the existing record `event:US-NVDA:ceo-resignation-2026-11` now has its sequel, the reinstatement (new event record). Two watch items:
  the Q3 FY27 10-Q (any disclosure of the SEC or California AG matters), and the independent committee's findings.
- **UTTAMSUGAR**: the L45 price calendar has been started (`research_notes/Deep dives/UTTAMSUGAR_price_calendar.md`). The next dated decision is the SC hearing on 2-Dec-2026.
  The UP SAP is still the largest open variable.
- **Live dives with an addendum**: UTTAMSUGAR (#8–#13) and UTKARSHBNK (#14–#15). INDRAMEDCO and SUNFLAG had nothing material confirmed.
- **Process lessons for the news layer**: (a) Google News re-surfaces stale items (Polycab "reserves order", the 2025 ICEMA safeguard plea).
  Before flagging, check the earliest-dated copy and the company's own filings. (b) Headline verbs overstate ("DOJ closes investigation" was an HSR
  expiry; "ousted" was a resignation accepted under pressure; "accounting practices" was a disclosure probe). (c) The RBI press-release
  archive (`BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=N`, sequential) is a cheap primary check for RBI meeting headlines.

| Business (Q2 FY27 sales `[DECK]`) | ₹ cr | Share | y/y | Unit / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Formulations: Europe | 186 | 19% | +22% | Alivira animal health: Spain (Karizoo 60%), Belgium/NL, Germany (Bremer), Sweden; BioForLife Italy from Q3 FY27 |
| Formulations: Emerging markets | 203 | 21% | +39% | Turkey (Provet, Topkim; Ind AS 29 hyperinflation), Brazil, Mexico; Vietnam entity registered |
| Formulations: India | 50 | 5% | +39% | own + distributed (BI companion-animal products) |
| Formulations: USA | 119 | 12% | **−11%** | Appco Pharma LLC (60%): human generics; exclusivity product eroded |
| APIs (human + animal) | 415 | 42% | +12% | 10 API sites (Hyderabad, Vizag ex-Mylan, Mahad, Vizag), 110+ APIs, CDMO |
| Other / Ind AS 29 | 14 | 1% | | |

- **Value chain:** KSMs/intermediates → API (own and third-party customers; backward integration for "key formulation products") → formulations (vet in EU/EM; human generics in US via Appco) → distributors/vets/pharmacies.
- **Peers with the same unit:** Granules, Neuland, Aarti Drugs, Solara (APIs). There is no clean listed Indian animal-health peer.
- **Flags:** cyclicality none (the API price cycle is mild); holdco none. The NCI structure is material: 40% of Appco and 40% of Karizoo belong to others.

body:
| Scenario | Path | Price | From today |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recovery | Fed pauses/cuts in 2027, central banks keep buying; bank targets hit | $4,150–4,650 by end-2027 | +14% to +28% |
| Range | Choppy, Fed-dependent | $3,300–4,200 through mid-2027 | −9% to +15% |
| **2011–15 repeat** | −45% from the record, then years flat | **~$3,070** | **−16%** |
| Severe (1980-style) | Sustained high real rates, central-bank buying stops | ~$2,000–2,250 (−60% to −65% from record) | **−38% to −45%** |

**Worst case I'd plan for: −16% from here (≈$3,070) as a realistic bad case, −40% (≈$2,100) as a tail that has happened before.**
The bigger risk is not the price but the **time**: after 2011 gold took 9 years to get back.

**In rupees it hurts less** if the rupee keeps weakening (+3–4%/yr historically), but a strong-dollar/Fed-hike phase also tends to
weaken the rupee, so a part of any dollar fall is cushioned, not removed.
